# Dimension: Harness Capability Matrix

Covers what each of the six harnesses does: tools, memory, skills/MCP,
subagents, providers and auth, license, version and governance. Sources are in
[citations.md](../citations.md). Everything is as of fetch date 2026-11-05.
"Not stated" means the fetched pages do not say. It does not mean the feature
is absent.

## Per-harness notes

### Hermes Agent

- Self-description: "the only agent with a built-in learning loop — it creates
  skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist
  knowledge, searches its own past conversations" [1].
- **Tool count conflicts between two vendor pages fetched the same day:** README
  says "40+ tools" [1]; docs index says "60+ built-in tools" [2]. Categories
  include web, terminal and file, browser, vision, delegate_task, memory,
  session_search and cronjob [3].
- Memory is bounded: MEMORY.md 2,200 chars (~800 tokens), USER.md 1,375 chars
  (~500 tokens), loaded as a "frozen snapshot at session start" [15].
- Skills load by progressive disclosure: the index costs ~3k tokens and full
  skill content loads on demand [14]. Skill-write approval is off by default
  [14]. The skill-write scanner is "off by default" [4].
- Versioning is mixed. v0.22.0 (2026-10-13) says "Hermes now ships tested
  SemVer releases", and earlier CalVer tags such as v2026.9.24 exist [16].
  Earlier 0.x numbers also appear: v0.13.0 in May 2026 [18], and 0.18.2–0.21.0
  in a September CVE [122]. How the two schemes related before v0.22.0 is not
  stated.
- Imports settings, memories and skills from Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and
  OpenClaw [1].

### OpenHands

- **The product line split.** The CLI repo says "This project is no longer
  actively maintained. We recommend using Agent Canvas" [41]. The local GUI is
  the "deprecated legacy local GUI" [42]. Current releases (v1.35.0) are Agent
  Canvas releases [46].
- Agent Canvas "is not responsible for… Providing the sandbox or workspace
  isolation layer" [43].
- Provider setup on the legacy page is by API key only. No subscription login is
  stated [42].

### opencode

- The repository owner is Anomaly. The `sst/opencode` URL renders as
  `anomalyco/opencode` [68], and the download page shows "© 2026 Anomaly" [66].
  A redirect is inferred from the rendered page; no HTTP status was captured.
- The agents page contradicts itself. It says "three built-in subagents" and
  also "two built-in subagents, General and Explore" [64].
- Anthropic subscriptions: the providers page says plugins for Claude Pro/Max
  exist, "Anthropic explicitly prohibits this", and they are no longer bundled
  as of 1.3.0 [63]. Release v2.2.3 (2026-10-30) adds a "Claude Agent" provider
  that uses "your Claude Code login" [67]. No fetched source says whether
  Anthropic approves this path.
- A v1.x line (v1.19.5) is still released alongside v2.x [67].

### Goose

- Governance moved: "Block has donated goose to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
  at the Linux Foundation" (2026-04-07) [76]. AAIF was announced 2025-12-09
  "with founding contributions from Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI" [77].
- ACP providers "use goose with your existing Claude Code or ChatGPT Plus/Pro
  subscriptions" [84]. The default `GOOSE_MODE` of auto maps to
  `bypassPermissions` for Claude and `agent-full-access` for Codex [84].
- Subagents run automatically in autonomous mode, which is the default, and are
  disabled in manual, smart and chat-only modes [78].

### Codex CLI

- Multi-agent tools (`spawn_agent`, `send_input`, etc.) are "stable; on by
  default". Memories are "off by default" [93].
- Signing in with an API key bills at standard API pricing instead of ChatGPT
  plan credits [92].

### Claude Code

- Proprietary: "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved." [109].
- Anthropic's restriction on third parties: "Unless previously approved,
  Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or
  rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent
  SDK." [105]. This bears on Hermes, opencode and Goose paths that route through
  a Claude subscription [4][67][84]. The prior topic
  [hermes-agent-k3s-openshell-billing](../../hermes-agent-k3s-openshell-billing/)
  covers billing in depth.

## Counter-evidence

1. **Hermes skill bloat.** Issue #22620 reports all installed skills injected
   every turn, "200+ skills… ~10-15K tokens to every single API call". A
   commenter measured ~4,024 tokens for 130 skills. Maintainers labelled it P3
   Low. The poster promotes a third-party product [19]. The current skills page describes progressive disclosure [14]. The
   fetched sources do not show whether that resolves the issue.
2. **Hermes memory limits.** A vendor that sells a competing memory provider says
   the ~2,200-char MEMORY.md drops "nuanced specifics" and FTS5 search "matches
   on exact keywords" [137]. Nous's own page confirms the bounds as by design
   [15].
3. **Harness vs model.** A preprint (not peer-reviewed) tested OpenCode, Codex
   CLI, Pi CLI and DeepAgents with open models over 52,168 trajectories. Its
   Cross-Model Fit scores are OpenCode 87.48, Pi CLI 77.13, Codex CLI 73.62 and
   DeepAgents 64.20, and it concludes "Harness rankings vary across models and
   benchmarks" [133]. It did not test Hermes, Goose, OpenHands or Claude Code.
   Widely repeated "same model, different harness" leaderboard figures [134]
   trace to a post whose author has since removed them, saying the comparison
   "did not establish matching model versions, task sets, settings, and source
   records" [135].
4. **Subscription friction.** The OpenCode–Claude Max controversy began with a
   GitHub issue "Why does OpenCode no longer work with the Claude Max plan?"
   [136].
5. **OpenHands resource limits.** Sandbox containers start "without any resource
   limits", which "can starve the main OpenHands app or cause the host machine
   to become unresponsive" (open issue) [52].
